thread:
pagerduty: PAGER: sev1 - increased node disk write latency on gpu-node-12 causing POD evictions in modelcache namespace. Trigger: kubelet eviction threshold exceeded. Autoescalate in 5m if not acknowledged.

infra-bot: Automated detection: /var/tmp usage > 92% on gpu-node-12, podooms=2, kubelet event: 'nodefs.eviction'. Candidate pods: modelcache-serve-3, modelcache-serve-4.

ryan-oncall: acked. I'm on it — pulling up node metrics and recent deploys. @sara.k can you check customer-facing alerts?

sara.k: on it. customer-alerts: two customers with elevated error rates for generation endpoints in us-west-2. I put a short status page note: "Investigating increased errors for inference - possible degraded capacity."

ben_d: looking at `kubectl get pods -n modelcache -o wide` - saw multiple CrashLoopBackOffs on modelcache pods, and one `OOMKilled`.

akshat: grabbing kernel logs: `ssh gpu-node-12` then `dmesg | tail -n 80` shows repeated `Blkd` writeback stalls and `EXT4-fs error` entries. Also CUDA driver warnings preceding container exits.

ryan-oncall: paste logs here.

akshat: ```
[ 12345.678901] sd 8:0:0:0: [sda] write cache full
[ 12345.679012] EXT4-fs (sda1): delayed write failed
[ 12345.682233] Out of memory: Killed process 21432 (modelcache) total-vm:1500000kB, anon-rss:1200000kB
[ 12345.682244] oom_reaper: reaped process 21432
[ 12345.690000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
```

infra-bot: node annotations: `kubelet.eviction.soft.nodefs.available` breached. Eviction threshold configured at 10GB free, available = 4.3GB. tmp volume `/var/tmp` responsible for most allocation (log spooling).

ryan-oncall: hypothesis: runaway checkpoint/log writes to tmp on node (possibly a misconfigured debug job or logging agent) filled ephemeral tmpvol, causing expensive writeback + IO stalls; kernel then starts killing high-mem containers -> model cache OOMs -> CUDA errors when processes restart.

ben_d: scanning pods writing to /var/tmp: `lsof | grep /var/tmp` shows `log-collector-ztl` (daemonset) and `debug-job-2026` (one-off). The debug-job is writing gzipped crash dumps every 10s — that's suspicious.

sara.k: CS update: two paying customers saw ~30% increase in 5xxs for ~7 minutes, one reported timed out requests. I've logged as "partial degradation".

ryan-oncall: mitigation plan: 1) cordon node gpu-node-12, 2) drain non-critical pods with `--ignore-daemonsets`, 3) identify runaway writer and stop it, 4) trigger modelcache pod restart on healthier node or scale up temporarily, 5) consider temporary increased eviction threshold or cleaning /var/tmp.

akshat: running `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12` now.

ben_d: cordon done. Starting `kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --force --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Will watch schedule.

infra-bot: Drain plan initiated: 12 pods to evict, 3 daemonsets ignored. Some pods unschedulable due to GPU requests; autoscaler not triggered because reserved capacity cap reached.

ryan-oncall: pause — want to avoid mass evictions that might cascade. Instead: 1) ssh and delete the debug-job container writing dumps; 2) manual cleanup of /var/tmp to recover space; 3) allow kubelet to re-evaluate eviction.

ben_d: found debug-job logs: it's an ad-hoc script with `while true; do tar czf /var/tmp/dump-$RANDOM.tgz /var/log/*.log; sleep 10; done`. Deleting job now.

akshat: deleted debug-job pod. Running `du -sh /var/tmp/* | sort -hr | head` — top is `dump-8343.tgz 18G`. Deleting those files.

infra-bot: Space freed: /var/tmp reduced from 92% -> 28%. Node eviction status cleared.

ryan-oncall: good. Monitoring node stability and modelcache pod restarts. Triggering rolling restart of modelcache-serve to recover KV cache, but keep one replica pinned to ensure capacity.

ben_d: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/modelcache-serve -n modelcache` initiated with `maxUnavailable=1`.

customer-success: FYI: customers previously impacted report requests recovering. Will update status page: "Mitigated - services recovering; root cause under investigation (temporary debug job filled /var/tmp)."

sara.k: note for postmortem: why did debug-job exist on prod node? who created it and why had elevated write rate? Also we need guardrails for jobs writing to node-local tmp (admission webhook?).

akshat: thrown in an immediate short-term guard: set a daemonset that cleans /var/tmp older than 5m on gpu nodes. Created PR for housekeeping cronjob.

ryan-oncall: handoff to infra SRE for post-incident root cause and long-term fixes. @ben_d @akshat please add any config changes to the incident ticket. I'll mark acknowledged -> resolved once metrics stable for 30m.

ben_d: adding notes and commands used to ticket:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl delete pod debug-job-xxxx -n infra
ssh gpu-node-12 'rm -rf /var/tmp/dump-*.tgz'
systemctl restart kubelet
kubectl rollout restart deployment/modelcache-serve -n modelcache
```

akshat: observed transient CUDA errors on restart but they recovered after pod reschedule; GPU drivers logged Xid 79. Suggest adding driver-resync alert threshold so kernel-level GPU disconnects trigger early paging.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by infra SRE. Pager cleared.

customer-success: status page updated: "Resolved - capacity restored. We are investigating cause (debug job filled node-local tmp)."

ryan-oncall: last check: 5xxs back to baseline, node free space stable ~45GB, no further evictions. Closing alert in 30m if no regression. Great response team. :thumbsup:

sara.k: taking postmortem lead. Assigning to infra team for follow-up items: cleanup cronjob, admission limit for node-local tmp writes, driver alerting, and better staging separation for debug jobs.

ben_d: noted. adding links to logs and kube events in the incident tracker.

akshat: optional - we should also add a predeploy admission check to deny pods with `hostPath: /var/tmp` write access unless explicitly whitelisted. Will prototype.

ryan-oncall: handing off to infra-bot for long-term tasks. Marking this thread as done for oncall rotation.

infra-bot: Follow-up checklist created in ticket #INC-2026: [cleanup cronjob], [admission webhook], [driver alerting], [postmortem doc].

pagerduty: Pager resolved at 4312346098.

customer-success: customers notified of root cause and remediation plan. Keep me looped on PM notes for status updates."
